children: Shares of On Semiconductor, which makes power management technology used in cars and artificial intelligence data centers, fell 9% Wednesday as its Investor Day disappointed investors, despite a big announcement.

The Scottsdale, Ariz.-based company said its new Embedded Power Platform, which is designed for use in AI data centers and electric cars for power switching, driving, and controlling, delivers three to five times more power density than current solutions.

Auto maker Subaru is one of Onsemi's first partners testing the new technology, which "is expected to begin sampling in 2026 with strategic customers and ecosystem participants across automotive and AI applications."
The new architecture "can redefine how power systems are built and create a new foundation for AI infrastructure, electrification and automation," Onsemi CEO Hassane El-Khoury said.

The Federal Reserve's decision to raise rates may also have hurt Onsemi, as higher rates increase the costs of the end products with its chips, including electrical cars and industrial equipment, which make up most of its revenue. The stock fell sharply after the Fed announced its rate decision, which hinged largely on curbing inflation.
Despite Wednesday's slide, Onsemi shares remain up 23% for the year, versus the tech-heavy Nasdaq, which is up just 12% by comparison.
The chip stock got a modest boost last month when its earnings beat analyst expectations and it raised guidance on revenue from sales to AI data centers.
